truth: On Sunday at six the clerk, Kit Sorrel, locks the silver cup in the vestry cupboard, locks the vestry door and takes its one key back to the sexton's lodge.
Amos Reed, the sexton, rings in the tower from six until nine, seen going up and coming down by the clerk in the porch. Mr. Vane, the curate, is at the Grange from five until half past nine.
Hester Dent signs the vestry key out at half past seven, takes the cup home to mend its foot, and signs the key back at a quarter past eight. The vestry has one door and barred windows.

frame.says: The cup was locked away at six and gone at nine; the vestry door was locked and its key taken back to the lodge.
Amos Reed went up the tower stair at six and came down at nine, seen from the porch, the stair's only end.
The vestry door has one key, kept in the lodge, and whoever borrows it signs the key book.

She signed it back at a quarter past eight; nobody else signed.
Mr. Vane sat at the Squire's bedside from five until half past nine.
The vestry has one door and barred windows.
